[Environmental economist · Pricing credibility in nature markets]{.lead-line}

## About

[I study whether nature markets deliver what they promise. On the demand side, I measure public support for forest conservation and carbon offsetting across Europe with discrete choice experiments. On the supply side, I price what a carbon credit actually delivers — net of leakage, storage duration, and reversal risk — with actuarial models and Monte Carlo simulation.]{.lead-line}

## Selected work

[**The Net Climate Value of Carbon Credits** — only 12–56% of a forest carbon credit survives as real climate value once leakage, storage duration, and reversal risk are priced together. [More →](research.qmd#net-climate-value)]{.meta}

[**Two Countries, One Divide** — fear of climate change splits public support for forest conservation the same way in Austria and France. [More →](research.qmd#two-countries-one-divide)]{.meta}

[**Classes or Continuum?** — a pre-registrable rule for specifying latent class choice models, implemented in the R package klue. [More →](research.qmd#classes-or-continuum)]{.meta}
